## How it works

- [statement] The ESR baseline places equality keys first, sort keys next, and range keys last when preserving index sort order is the priority. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: ESR guideline and $in placement in compound indexes · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/ten-recommendations-for-running-your-mongodb-environment/, https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md, https://ozgurgurcan.com/blog/mongodb-compound-indexes-esr-rule, https://percona.university/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/MongoDB-Performance-issues-Troubleshooting-methods-2.pdf

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The documented 201-or-more case treats $in as range-like for sorting: subsequent index keys cannot supply the requested sort. Place typically large lists with range fields when designing for ESR. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: ESR guideline and $in placement in compound indexes · also: https://dev.to/mongodb/or-expansion-in-mongodb-and-how-in-is-treated-as-a-range-with-skip-scan-or-an-equality-for-2b38
- [statement] The 201-element boundary is not guaranteed across versions; the historical SERVER-14034 fix raised the scan-expansion limit from 50 to 200 in MongoDB 2.6.4. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: ESR guideline and $in placement in compound indexes · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-14034

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] ERS can outperform ESR when a selective range reduces enough work to justify a blocking sort; ESR is a guideline rather than a universal optimum. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: ESR guideline and $in placement in compound indexes · also: https://dev.to/mongodb/or-expansion-in-mongodb-and-how-in-is-treated-as-a-range-with-skip-scan-or-an-equality-for-2b38, https://ozgurgurcan.com/blog/mongodb-compound-indexes-esr-rule
- [statement] Validate index placement with explain('executionStats') on representative queries and list sizes. Inspect SORT versus SORT_MERGE and compare keys and documents examined instead of assuming that IXSCAN alone proves sort support. (medium confidence) — https://dev.to/mongodb/or-expansion-in-mongodb-and-how-in-is-treated-as-a-range-with-skip-scan-or-an-equality-for-2b38 · keywords: ESR guideline and $in placement in compound indexes · also: https://github.com/OneUptime/blog/blob/master/posts/2026-01-30-mongodb-compound-index-strategies/README.md, https://www.percona.com/blog/ten-recommendations-for-running-your-mongodb-environment/
- [statement] For sort-bearing queries, place typically small $in lists with equality predicates and typically large lists with range predicates; verify the plan rather than treating $in as unconditional equality. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: ESR guideline and $in placement in compound indexes · also: https://ozgurgurcan.com/blog/mongodb-compound-indexes-esr-rule
- [statement] Compare candidate index orders using hint() and explain('executionStats'); inspect SORT versus SORT_MERGE and compare keys/documents examined with rows returned. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: ESR guideline and $in placement in compound indexes · also: https://ozgurgurcan.com/blog/mongodb-compound-indexes-esr-rule

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Equality keys can appear in any relative order for a query that constrains all of them to exact values. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: ESR guideline and $in placement in compound indexes · also: https://ozgurgurcan.com/blog/mongodb-compound-indexes-esr-rule
- [statement] For eligible sorted queries, the documented small-list case is fewer than 201 $in elements: ordered index scans can feed SORT_MERGE, making the $in key equality-like before the sort keys. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: ESR guideline and $in placement in compound indexes · also: https://dev.to/mongodb/or-expansion-in-mongodb-and-how-in-is-treated-as-a-range-with-skip-scan-or-an-equality-for-2b38
- [statement] SERVER-14034 documents multiplication across $in prefixes: ten values on a and six on b require 60 scans for sorting c under {a:1,b:1,c:1}. That exceeded the historical 50-scan cap; small individual lists therefore did not guarantee expansion. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-14034
- [statement] $in alone performs equality matches; with sorting, short lists can be expanded and combined through SORT_MERGE, while long lists behave like ranges for index ordering. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md · keywords: ESR guideline and $in placement in compound indexes · also: https://ozgurgurcan.com/blog/mongodb-compound-indexes-esr-rule
- [statement] The MongoDB guide documents fewer than 201 $in elements as expandable with sort, and 201 or more as range-like, preventing subsequent index fields from supplying sort. It explicitly warns this cutoff can vary across versions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md
